title: Plurals that break the rules
goal: Use the right plural, and know which words are always plural
intro: Most plurals just add -s. But some nouns change completely (child → children), some are always plural (trousers, scissors), and some look plural but aren’t (news, mathematics). Numbers used as adjectives never take -s: a five-star hotel.

examples: a man, two men; a person, many people

rules.rule: Pairs are always plural: trousers, jeans, scissors, glasses, pants.
A number joined to a noun before another noun stays singular.
After “one of”, use a plural noun.

mistakes.wrong: One of my friend is a doctor.
mistakes.right: One of my friends is a doctor.
mistakes.why: After “one of” the noun is plural.

mistakes.right: I bought new jeans. / I bought a new pair of jeans.

mistakes.why: Before a noun, the number phrase stays singular.

mistakes.wrong: Many peoples came to the party.
mistakes.right: Many people came to the party.

ex.q: She is one of my closest ___.

ex.y: Before a noun, the number phrase stays singular.

ex.q: How many ___ work in your office?

ex.y: The plural of child is children.

ex.q: We took a two-hours flight to Goa.
ex.fixed: We took a two-hour flight to Goa.
ex.y: Before a noun: a two-hour flight.

ex.q: One of the student was absent.
ex.fixed: One of the students was absent.

ex.q: I need a new pair of ___. (jeans / jean)

ex.a: It is one of the best films I have seen.
ex.y: one of + the best + plural noun

talk: Describe your family and the people in your office or class. Use “one of…”, and plurals like children, people, and women.
